## Three parts, one remote

::: {.qr-cards}
::: {.qr-card}
<i class="bi bi-filetype-md qr-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i>

### Quarto extension

Give each slide a time (or not). A countdown in the speaker view, pause and reset keys. Free and open source.

[The extension →](extension.qmd)
:::

::: {.qr-card}
<i class="bi bi-phone qr-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i>

### iPhone & Apple Watch

Next and back, your notes, the countdown, and whether you are ahead of schedule. The watch buzzes when time is up.

[The apps →](apps.qmd#iphone)
:::

::: {.qr-card}
<i class="bi bi-laptop qr-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i>

### QRemote Relay for Mac

Lives in the menu bar and links the presentation open in your browser to your remotes. Nothing to configure.

[QRemote Relay →](apps.qmd#qremote-relay-mac)
:::
:::

## How it works

::: {.qr-steps}
1. **Add the extension** to your presentation: `quarto add Nenuial/quarto-qremote`, then `revealjs-plugins: [qremote]` in the YAML header. Give slides a time if you like: `## My slide {timing="45"}`.
2. **Open QRemote Relay** on the Mac that shows the presentation, then open the rendered presentation in your browser. It connects on its own.
3. **Open QRemote** on your iPhone: it finds your Mac. Your Apple Watch uses the iPhone's settings. Go!
:::

```{=html}
<figure class="qr-flow" aria-label="The iPhone and Apple Watch talk to QRemote Relay on the Mac, which talks to the presentation in the browser on the same Mac, over the local network only">
  <div class="qr-flow-row">
    <div class="qr-node"><i class="bi bi-phone" aria-hidden="true"></i><strong>iPhone</strong><span>Apple Watch</span></div>
    <i class="bi bi-arrow-left-right qr-arrow" aria-hidden="true"></i>
    <div class="qr-node qr-node-relay"><i class="bi bi-laptop" aria-hidden="true"></i><strong>QRemote Relay</strong><span>menu bar of your Mac</span></div>
    <i class="bi bi-arrow-left-right qr-arrow" aria-hidden="true"></i>
    <div class="qr-node"><i class="bi bi-easel" aria-hidden="true"></i><strong>Presentation</strong><span>browser, same Mac</span></div>
  </div>
  <figcaption><i class="bi bi-house-lock" aria-hidden="true"></i> Local network only: nothing goes to the internet</figcaption>
</figure>
```

## Made for timed talks

Pitches, PechaKucha, lessons, conference talks: anywhere the clock matters. Each slide can have its own time; slides without one simply show how long you have spent on them. The speaker view shows where you should be by the end of each slide, and the iPhone shows whether you are ahead of or behind schedule.

No account, no cloud, no data collected: everything stays on your local network. [Privacy](privacy.qmd).

::: {.qr-note}
The iPhone, Apple Watch and Mac apps are coming soon to the App Store. The Quarto extension works on its own today, as a speaker-view timer.
:::
